note: Every number below was read from the study abstract by hand and checked against it. Diagnostic delay means time from first symptom to diagnosis unless the measure says otherwise.

searched.query: each condition's search terms AND ("diagnostic delay" OR "time to diagnosis" OR misdiagnosis OR misdiagnosed), PubMed-indexed
searched.alsoRead: All 89 R-CPD abstracts, and every A-CPD, Zenker's and spasm abstract mentioning symptom duration

conditions.headline: About 17 years
conditions.headlineDetail: Symptoms began at a mean age of 13.6 and diagnosis came at a mean age of 30.4, in one clinic series of 106 patients.

rows.measure: Mean age at first symptoms vs at diagnosis
rows.caveat: Two group averages, not each person's own wait. Patients who reach a specialist clinic may have waited longer than most.

rows.design: 5 studies that recorded how the diagnosis was made, within a systematic review
rows.caveat: About 450 patients in those 5 studies. Pooled from uncontrolled studies.

rows.measure: First learned the name on social media
rows.caveat: Small and not designed to give a percentage, but unanimous.

rows.measure: A doctor put the symptoms down to reflux
rows.design: Online survey of an R-CPD community

rows.measure: Given a different diagnosis before seeing a specialist (children)

conditions.headline: Not measured
conditions.headlineDetail: No study in the search measured how long it takes to diagnose. The only figure is a symptom duration from a 1980 surgical series.

rows.caveat: Written before modern definitions. 30% of these patients also had a Zenker's pouch.

conditions.headline: About 2 years
conditions.headlineDetail: Median 24 months in a recent Italian study of 278 patients. Our search found six studies of diagnostic delay in adults and children.

rows.caveat: 42% had at least one wrong diagnosis first (26% one, 16% more than one), most often reflux (16.7%).
Older data; no shortening over the period studied.
Longer waits went with more unsuccessful doctor visits, not with unusual symptoms.
Standard deviation 33 months, so a wide spread.

conditions.headline: Not measured
conditions.headlineDetail: Only one small study (28 patients) reports a delay before diagnosis. Other small treatment series give how long symptoms had lasted.

rows.design: Case series of a new endoscopic technique

rows.caveat: Includes 5 patients with a different kind of pouch.

conditions.headline: Not measured
conditions.headlineDetail: No study in the search measured diagnostic delay. One small POEM series mentions symptom duration.

rows.caveat: Thirteen patients, measured at treatment rather than diagnosis.
